name: answer for tomorrow, then fold the page over
one_line: Three answers about tomorrow written today, folded out of sight along a printed line, and opened tomorrow beside what actually happened.
how: Three questions about the same hour tomorrow, filled in now: what will be in the kitchen, who will come in first, one thing that will have moved by itself. Then a dotted line across the sheet with «fold here» on it. The fold is the only mechanism: it stops the answers being adjusted without anybody watching. Below it, the second half — open the page and write beside each one what happened. Make one question slightly absurd, because an absurd question buys a whole day of attention. Last line: the one you got most wrong is the interesting one, ring it and write in one line why you thought otherwise.

knobs.knob: whether the answers are written first
knobs.effect: Written and folded away, a wrong guess stays wrong and is a fact; recalled the next day, memory tidies it, everything was obvious all along, and the day taught nobody anything.
Ten seconds is settled while you watch and needs no fold; a day is long enough for a guess to be a guess and short enough that the sheet is still around; a year does not come back.

knobs.knob: whether reasons are asked for before looking
knobs.effect: The canonical form has four boxes and not three, and the extra one holds the reasons written before the observation; without them a wrong prediction cannot be explained afterwards without inventing why.

Pointed at the house — who comes in first, what will have moved — anybody can answer and the answers get settled; pointed at the reader — how long I will take, how hard it will be — it produces a number about a person.

where_the_work_is: In the fold. It makes the first half unalterable with nobody supervising, and the same three questions without it are three opinions written down and quietly revised.
breaks: It is a form in two parts and nothing brings the second part back; a sheet found a week later holds three predictions and no outcomes, which is a whole afternoon returning empty. A folded sheet scans with a crease across it that can cut through a line of handwriting. On a display the three questions fit and the fold does not exist.
